selectedBlocks.text: باب التطوع بعد المكتوبة

[1119] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد عن عبيد الله قال: أخبرنا نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال صليت مع النبي ﷺ سجدتين قبل الظهر وسجدتين بعد الظهر وسجدتين بعد المغرب وسجدتين بعد العشاء وسجدتين بعد الجمعة فأما المغرب والعشاء ففي بيته وحدثتني أختي حفصة أن النبي ﷺ كان يصلي سجدتين خفيفتين بعد ما يطلع الفجر وكانت ساعة لا أدخل على النبي ﷺ فيها، وقال ابن أبي الزناد عن موسى بن عقبة عن نافع بعد العشاء في أهله تابعه كثير بن فرقد وأيوب عن نافع
باب من لم يتطوع بعد المكتوبة

[1120] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان عن عمرو قال: سمعت أبا الشعثاء جابرا قال: سمعت ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال صليت مع رسول الله ﷺ ثمانيا جميعا وسبعا جميعا قلت: يا أبا الشعثاء أظنه أخر الظهر وعجل العصر وعجل العشاء وأخر المغرب قال وأنا أظنه
باب صلاة الضحى في السفر
[1121] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن شعبة عن توبة عن مورق قال: قلت لابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما أتصلي الضحى قال لا قلت: فعمر قال لا قلت: فأبو بكر قال لا قلت: فالنبي ﷺ قال لا إخاله

[1122] حدثنا آدم حدثنا شعبة حدثنا عمرو بن مرة قال: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى يقول: ما حدثنا أحد أنه رأى النبي ﷺ يصلي الضحى غير أم هانئ فإنها قالت إن النبي ﷺ دخل بيتها يوم فتح مكة فاغتسل وصلى ثماني ركعات فلم أر صلاة قط أخف منها غير أنه يتم الركوع والسجود
باب من لم يصل الضحى ورآه واسعا
[1123] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب عن الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت ما رأيت رسول الله ﷺ سبح سبحة الضحى وإني لأسبحها
باب صلاة الضحى في الحضر
قاله عتبان بن مالك عن النبي ﷺ

[1124] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم أخبرنا شعبة حدثنا عباس الجريري هو ابن فروخ عن أبي عثمان النهدي عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال أوصاني خليلي بثلاث لا أدعهن حتى أموت صوم ثلاثة أيام من كل شهر وصلاة الضحى ونوم على وتر

[1125] حدثنا علي بن الجعد أخبرنا شعبة عن أنس بن سيرين قال: سمعت أنس بن مالك الأنصارى قال: قال رجل من الأنصار وكان ضخما للنبي ﷺ إني لا أستطيع الصلاة معك فصنع للنبي ﷺ طعاما فدعاه إلى بيته ونضح له طرف حصير بماء فصلى عليه ركعتين، وقال: فلان بن فلان بن جارود لأنس رضى الله تعالى عنه أكان النبي ﷺ يصلي الضحى، فقال: ما رأيته صلى غير ذلك اليوم
باب الركعتين قبل الظهر

[1126] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال حفظت من النبي ﷺ عشر ركعات ركعتين قبل الظهر وركعتين بعدها وركعتين بعد المغرب في بيته وركعتين بعد العشاء في بيته وركعتين قبل صلاة الصبح كانت ساعة لا يدخل على النبي ﷺ فيها حدثتني حفصة أنه كان إذا إذن المؤذن وطلع الفجر صلى ركعتين
[1127] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن شعبة عن إبراهيم بن محمد بن المنتشر عن أبيه عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها أن النبي ﷺ كان لا يدع أربعا قبل الظهر وركعتين قبل الغداة تابعه بن أبي عدي وعمرو عن شعبة
باب الصلاة قبل المغرب
[1128] حدثنا أبو معمر حدثنا عبد الوارث عن الحسين عن ابن بريدة قال: حدثني عبد الله المزني عن النبي ﷺ قال: صلوا قبل صلاة المغرب قال في الثالثة لمن شاء كراهية أن يتخذها الناس سنة

[1129] حدثنا عبد الله بن يزيد قال: حدثنا سعيد بن أبي أيوب قال: حدثني يزيد بن أبي حبيب قال: سمعت مرثد بن عبد الله اليزني قال أتيت عقبة بن عامر الجهني فقلت: ألا أعجبك من أبي تميم يركع ركعتين قبل صلاة المغرب، فقال عقبة إنا كنا نفعله على عهد رسول الله ﷺ قلت: فما يمنعك الآن قال الشغل
باب صلاة النوافل جماعة
ذكره أنس وعائشة رضى الله تعالى عنهما عن النبي ﷺ

[1130] حدثني إسحاق حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم حدثنا أبي عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني محمود بن الربيع الأنصارى أنه عقل رسول الله ﷺ وعقل مجة مجها في وجهه من بئر كانت في دارهم فزعم محمود أنه سمع عتبان بن مالك الأنصارى رضى الله تعالى عنه وكان ممن شهد بدرا مع رسول الله ﷺ يقول: كنت أصلي لقومي ببني سالم وكان يحول بيني وبينهم واد إذا جاءت الأمطار فيشق علي اجتيازه قبل مسجدهم فجئت رسول الله ﷺ فقلت له إني أنكرت بصري وإن الوادي الذي بيني وبين قومي يسيل إذا جاءت الأمطار فيشق علي اجتيازه فوددت أنك تأتي فتصلي من بيتي مكانا أتخذه مصلى، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: سأفعل فغدا علي رسول الله ﷺ وأبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه بعد ما اشتد النهار فاستأذن رسول الله ﷺ فأذنت له فلم يجلس حتى قال أين تحب أن أصلي من بيتك فأشرت له إلى المكان الذي أحب أن أصلي فيه فقام رسول الله ﷺ فكبر وصففنا وراءه فصلى ركعتين ثم سلم وسلمنا حين سلم فحبسته على خزير يصنع له فسمع أهل الدار رسول الله ﷺ في بيتي فثاب رجال منهم حتى كثر الرجال في البيت، فقال رجل منهم ما فعل مالك لا أراه، فقال رجل منهم ذاك منافق لا يحب الله ورسوله، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: لا تقل ذاك ألا تراه قال لا إله إلا الله يبتغي بذلك وجه الله، فقال الله ورسوله أعلم أما نحن فوالله لا نرى وده ولا حديثه إلا إلى المنافقين قال رسول الله ﷺ: فإن الله قد حرم على النار من قال لا إله إلا الله يبتغي بذلك وجه الله قال محمود فحدثتها قوما فيهم أبو أيوب صاحب رسول الله ﷺ في غزوته التي توفي فيها ويزيد بن معاوية عليهم بأرض الروم فأنكرها على أبو أيوب قال والله ما أظن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ما قلت: قط فكبر ذلك علي فجعلت لله علي إن سلمني حتى أقفل من غزوتي أن أسأل عنها عتبان بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه إن وجدته حيا في مسجد قومه فقفلت فأهللت بحجة أو بعمرة ثم سرت حتى قدمت المدينة فأتيت بني سالم فإذا عتبان شيخ أعمى يصلي لقومه فلما سلم من الصلاة سلمت عليه وأخبرته من أنا ثم سألته عن ذلك الحديث فحدثنيه كما حدثنيه أول مرة
باب التطوع في البيت
[1131] حدثنا عبد الأعلى بن حماد حدثنا وهيب عن أيوب وعبيد الله عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: اجعلوا في بيوتكم من صلاتكم ولا تتخذوها قبورا تابعه عبد الوهاب عن أيوب

segments.arabic: [1119] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد عن عبيد الله قال: أخبرنا نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah. He said: Nafi‘ informed us, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت مع النبي ﷺ سجدتين قبل الظهر وسجدتين بعد الظهر وسجدتين بعد المغرب وسجدتين بعد العشاء وسجدتين بعد الجمعة فأما المغرب والعشاء ففي بيته وحدثتني أختي حفصة أن النبي ﷺ كان يصلي سجدتين خفيفتين بعد ما يطلع الفجر وكانت ساعة لا أدخل على النبي ﷺ فيها،
segments.english: I prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, two rak‘ahs before Dhuhr, two rak‘ahs after Dhuhr, two rak‘ahs after Maghrib, two rak‘ahs after ‘Isha’, and two rak‘ahs after Jumu‘ah. As for Maghrib and ‘Isha’, they were in his house. My sister Hafsah related to me that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray two brief rak‘ahs after dawn appeared. It was an hour when I did not enter upon the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

segments.arabic: وقال ابن أبي الزناد عن موسى بن عقبة عن نافع بعد العشاء في أهله تابعه كثير بن فرقد وأيوب عن نافع
segments.english: And Ibn Abi al-Zinad said, from Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Nafi‘: “After ‘Isha’, with his family.” Kathir ibn Farqad and Ayyub corroborated it from Nafi‘.

comparisons.note: The Hafsah passage and the family-at-Isha wording are rearranged, while the named Ibn Abi al-Zinad/Musa ibn Uqbah route and Kathir ibn Farqad/Ayyub corroboration are abbreviated. Do not use this comparison to reconstruct the complete selected closing routes.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn 'Umar:

I offered with the Prophet two Rakat before the Zuhr and two Rakat after the Zuhr prayer; two Rakat after Maghrib, Isha' and the Jumua prayers. Those of the Maghrib and 'Isha' were offered in his house. My sister Hafsa told me that the Prophet used to offer two light Rakat after dawn and it was the time when I never went to the Prophet."
comparisons.note: The complete closing Ibn Abi al-Zinad/Musa ibn Uqbah/Nafi route and Kathir ibn Farqad/Ayyub corroboration are absent.

notes: The complete five-pair account, Hafsah passage and both closing routes occupy one selected paragraph. Modern 1172/1173 split and repeat closing material; all selected passages remain one app reference.

All five pairs, the Hafsah continuation and both complete closing routes remain in selected order. Sajdatayn is rendered as two rakahs in this prayer context, as Fath al-Bari explicitly explains; it is not rendered as two isolated prostrations. The final with-his-family wording is retained rather than replaced by in-his-house.

After the Hafsah passage, the historical and modern closing routes appear in the opposite order to the selected digital paragraph. Modern 1172 also has closing material before the separately numbered Hafsah continuation. Preserve the selected sequence; do not duplicate printed overlap.

segments.arabic: [1120] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان عن عمرو قال: سمعت أبا الشعثاء جابرا قال: سمعت ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Amr, who said: I heard Abu al-Sha‘tha’, Jabir, say: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, say:

segments.arabic: صليت مع رسول الله ﷺ ثمانيا جميعا وسبعا جميعا
segments.english: I prayed with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, eight together and seven together.

segments.arabic: قلت: يا أبا الشعثاء أظنه أخر الظهر وعجل العصر وعجل العشاء وأخر المغرب قال وأنا أظنه
segments.english: I said, “Abu al-Sha‘tha’, I think he delayed Dhuhr and brought ‘Asr forward, and brought ‘Isha’ forward and delayed Maghrib.” He said, “I think so too.”

comparisons.note: Prayer names are supplied in the initial eight/seven-unit statement. The selected statement gives the counts together without those parenthetical identifications.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Amr:

I heard Abu Ash-sha'tha' Jabir saying, "I heard Ibn Abbas saying, 'I offered with Allah's Apostle eight Rakat (of Zuhr and 'Asr prayers) together and seven Rakat (the Maghrib and the 'Isha' prayers) together.' " I said, "O Abu Ash-shatha! I think he must have prayed the Zuhr late and the 'Asr early; the 'Isha early and the Maghrib late." Abu Ash-sha'tha' said, "I also think so." (See Hadith No. 518 Vol. 1).
comparisons.note: The opening eight/seven-unit statement supplies parenthetical prayer names absent from that selected clause.

notes: Keep the eight-together/seven-together statement and the full later question and answer. The order of the Isha and Maghrib timing clauses stays as selected.

The opening counts stay eight together and seven together without inserted prayer names. The final question is Amr’s exchange with Abu al-Shatha, as both English comparisons make explicit; the selected text does not repeat Amr’s name there, so no name is inserted into the translation. Both timing clauses retain their source order and uncertainty.

segments.arabic: [1121] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن شعبة عن توبة عن مورق قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Tawbah, from Muwarriq, who said:

segments.arabic: قلت لابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما أتصلي الضحى قال لا قلت: فعمر قال لا قلت: فأبو بكر قال لا قلت: فالنبي ﷺ قال لا إخاله
segments.english: I said to Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, “Do you pray Duha?” He said, “No.” I said, “And ‘Umar?” He said, “No.” I said, “And Abu Bakr?” He said, “No.” I said, “And the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” He said, “I do not think so.”

segments.arabic: [1122] حدثنا آدم حدثنا شعبة حدثنا عمرو بن مرة قال: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى يقول:
segments.english: Adam related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. ‘Amr ibn Murrah related to us. He said: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla say:

segments.arabic: ما حدثنا أحد أنه رأى النبي ﷺ يصلي الضحى غير أم هانئ فإنها قالت إن النبي ﷺ دخل بيتها يوم فتح مكة فاغتسل وصلى ثماني ركعات فلم أر صلاة قط أخف منها غير أنه يتم الركوع والسجود
segments.english: No one related to us that he had seen the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray Duha except Umm Hani’. She said that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered her house on the day Mecca was conquered, bathed, and prayed eight rak‘ahs. “I never saw a prayer lighter than it, yet he completed the bowing and prostration.”

comparisons.note: The selected lighter-prayer wording is rendered as more rudimentary. Preserve both the lightness comparison and the completion of bowing and prostration without importing that characterization.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Abdur Rahman bin Abi Laila:

Only Um Hani narrated to me that she had seen the Prophet offering the Duha prayer. She said, "On the day of the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet entered my house, took a bath and offered eight Rakat (of Duha prayers. I had never seen the Prophet offering such a light prayer but he performed bowing and prostrations perfectly .
comparisons.note: The selected no-one-informed-us construction becomes narrated-to-me. The English also supplies Duha in a parenthesis after the eight units.

notes: Keep both Prophet honorifics, entry into her home, bathing, eight units, lightness and completed bowing/prostration. Preserve the selected us and the shift to her first-person observation.

The complete to-us reporting, both Prophet honorifics, entry, bathing, eight units, first-person observation, lightness and completed bowing/prostration remain. Quotation marks show the source shift from her house to I never saw; they add no explanatory wording.
The historical route uses reported-to-me where selected and modern use reported-to-us. Preserve the selected reporting person.

segments.arabic: [1123] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب عن الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: ما رأيت رسول الله ﷺ سبح سبحة الضحى وإني لأسبحها
segments.english: I did not see the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform the voluntary Duha prayer, but I do perform it.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Aisha:
I never saw the Prophet offering the Duha prayer but I always offer it.
comparisons.note: The selected Messenger of Allah is rendered as Prophet; always is added to the final statement about performing the prayer.

segments.arabic: [1124] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم أخبرنا شعبة حدثنا عباس الجريري هو ابن فروخ عن أبي عثمان النهدي عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. Shu‘bah informed us. ‘Abbas al-Jurayri—he is Ibn Farrukh—related to us, from Abu ‘Uthman al-Nahdi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: أوصاني خليلي بثلاث لا أدعهن حتى أموت صوم ثلاثة أيام من كل شهر وصلاة الضحى ونوم على وتر
segments.english: My close friend advised me to do three things that I will not give up until I die: fasting three days of each month, the Duha prayer, and sleeping after Witr.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Huraira:
My friend (the Prophet) advised me to do three things and I shall not leave them till I die, these are: To fast three days every month, to offer the Duha prayer, and to offer Witr before sleeping.
comparisons.note: The identification the Prophet is supplied in parentheses after my friend, although it is not explicit in this selected occurrence.

notes: Keep Abbas al-Jurayri identified as Ibn Farrukh in the selected chain. All three recommendations and the until-death commitment remain; the historical witness has a different identification and additional honorific.

segments.arabic: [1125] حدثنا علي بن الجعد أخبرنا شعبة عن أنس بن سيرين قال: سمعت أنس بن مالك الأنصارى قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn al-Ja‘d related to us. Shu‘bah informed us, from Anas ibn Sirin, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik al-Ansari say:

segments.arabic: قال رجل من الأنصار وكان ضخما للنبي ﷺ إني لا أستطيع الصلاة معك فصنع للنبي ﷺ طعاما فدعاه إلى بيته ونضح له طرف حصير بماء فصلى عليه ركعتين،
segments.english: A man of the Ansar, who was heavily built, said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “I am unable to pray with you.” He prepared food for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, invited him to his house, and sprinkled the edge of a mat with water for him. He prayed two rak‘ahs on it.

segments.arabic: وقال: فلان بن فلان بن جارود لأنس رضى الله تعالى عنه أكان النبي ﷺ يصلي الضحى، فقال: ما رأيته صلى غير ذلك اليوم
segments.english: So-and-so, son of so-and-so, son of Jarud, said to Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray Duha?” He said, “I did not see him pray it except on that day.”

checkedBody: Narrated Anas bin Sirin:

I heard Anas bin Malik al-Ansari saying, "An Ansari man, who was very fat, said to the Prophet, 'I am unable to present myself for the prayer with you.' He prepared a meal for the Prophet and invited him to his house. He washed one side of a mat with water and the Prophet offered two Rakat on it." So and so, the son of so and so, the son of Al-Jarud asked Anas, "Did the Prophet use to offer the Duha prayer?" Anas replied, "I never saw him praying (the Duha prayer) except on that day."
comparisons.note: The selected sprinkling of the mat is rendered as washing, and the name Jarud gains the definite article. The comparison supplies a Duha parenthesis in the closing answer. Its distinct displayed label 275t must not be confused with the following 275 entry.

segments.arabic: [1126] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: حفظت من النبي ﷺ عشر ركعات ركعتين قبل الظهر وركعتين بعدها وركعتين بعد المغرب في بيته وركعتين بعد العشاء في بيته وركعتين قبل صلاة الصبح كانت ساعة لا يدخل على النبي ﷺ فيها
segments.english: I remembered ten rak‘ahs from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: two rak‘ahs before Dhuhr and two after it, two rak‘ahs after Maghrib in his house, two rak‘ahs after ‘Isha’ in his house, and two rak‘ahs before the dawn prayer. It was an hour when no one would enter upon the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

segments.arabic: حدثتني حفصة أنه كان إذا إذن المؤذن وطلع الفجر صلى ركعتين
segments.english: Hafsah related to me that when the caller gave the call to prayer and dawn had appeared, he would pray two rak‘ahs.

comparisons.note: The selected in-his-house phrase after Isha is absent, although the house phrase after Maghrib remains.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn 'Umar:
I remember ten Rakat of Nawafil from the Prophet, two Rakat before the Zuhr prayer and two after it; two Rakat after Maghrib prayer in his house, and two Rakat after 'Isha' prayer in his

house, and two Rakat before the Fajr prayer and at that time nobody would enter the house of the Prophet Hafsa told me that the Prophet used to offer two Rakat after the call maker had made the Adhan and the day had dawned.
comparisons.note: The explanation of Nawafil and an explicit house object in the no-entry clause are supplied. Retain the selected clauses without importing those expansions.

segments.arabic: [1127] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن شعبة عن إبراهيم بن محمد بن المنتشر عن أبيه عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان لا يدع أربعا قبل الظهر وركعتين قبل الغداة
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never left out four before Dhuhr and two rak‘ahs before the morning prayer.

segments.arabic: تابعه بن أبي عدي وعمرو عن شعبة
segments.english: Ibn Abi ‘Adi and ‘Amr corroborated it from Shu‘bah.

checkedBody: Narrated Aisha:
The Prophet never missed four Rakat before the Zuhr prayer and two Rakat before the Fajr prayer.

segments.arabic: [1128] حدثنا أبو معمر حدثنا عبد الوارث عن الحسين عن ابن بريدة قال: حدثني عبد الله المزني عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from al-Husayn, from Ibn Buraydah, who said: ‘Abdullah al-Muzani related to me, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: صلوا قبل صلاة المغرب قال في الثالثة لمن شاء
segments.english: “Pray before the Maghrib prayer.” On the third time he said, “For whoever wishes.”

segments.arabic: كراهية أن يتخذها الناس سنة
segments.english: Out of dislike that people should take it as a sunnah.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Abdullah Al-Muzni:

The Prophet said, "Pray before the Maghrib (compulsory) prayer." He (said it thrice) and in the third time, he said, "Whoever wants to offer it can do so." He said so because he did not like the people to take it as a tradition.
comparisons.note: The comparison supplies compulsory and an explanatory said-it-thrice parenthesis. Retain the actual quoted wording and the third-time qualifier without adding duplicated quotations.

notes: Keep the third-time qualification and the closing sunna clause. Neither a legal ruling nor repeated quotation text is supplied by this intake.

segments.arabic: [1129] حدثنا عبد الله بن يزيد قال: حدثنا سعيد بن أبي أيوب قال: حدثني يزيد بن أبي حبيب قال: سمعت مرثد بن عبد الله اليزني قال
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid related to us. He said: Sa‘id ibn Abi Ayyub related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Abi Habib related to me. He said: I heard Marthad ibn ‘Abdullah al-Yazani say:

segments.arabic: أتيت عقبة بن عامر الجهني فقلت: ألا أعجبك من أبي تميم يركع ركعتين قبل صلاة المغرب، فقال عقبة إنا كنا نفعله على عهد رسول الله ﷺ قلت: فما يمنعك الآن قال الشغل
segments.english: I came to ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir al-Juhani and said, “Shall I not tell you something surprising about Abu Tamim? He prays two rak‘ahs before the Maghrib prayer.” ‘Uqbah said, “We used to do that in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” I said, “What prevents you now?” He said, “Being occupied.”

comparisons.note: The selected honorific following the Messenger of Allah is absent in this comparison body. Business is a narrower rendering of the closing occupation/preoccupation wording.

checkedBody: Narrated Marthad bin 'Abdullah Al-Yazani:

I went to 'Uqba bin 'Amir Al-Juhani and said, "Is it not surprising that Abi Tamim offers two Rakat before the Maghrib prayer?" 'Uqba said, "We used to do so in the life-time of Allah's Apostle." I asked him, "What prevents you from offering it now?" He replied, "Business."
comparisons.note: Business narrows the selected closing occupation/preoccupation wording.

notes: Preserve the complete Marthad/Uqbah exchange and its closing reason. Historical chain identifications and Prophet designation differ from the selected source.

The full question-and-answer exchange remains. The selected al-Yazani and al-Juhani identifications are retained without importing additional narrator identifications. Being occupied avoids narrowing the final word to commercial business.

segments.arabic: [1130] حدثني إسحاق حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم حدثنا أبي عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني محمود بن الربيع الأنصارى
segments.english: Ishaq related to me. Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. My father related to us, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ al-Ansari informed me:

segments.arabic: أنه عقل رسول الله ﷺ وعقل مجة مجها في وجهه من بئر كانت في دارهم
segments.english: He remembered the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and remembered a mouthful of water that the Messenger sprayed into his face from a well that was in their house.

segments.arabic: فزعم محمود أنه سمع عتبان بن مالك الأنصارى رضى الله تعالى عنه وكان ممن شهد بدرا مع رسول الله ﷺ يقول: كنت أصلي لقومي ببني سالم وكان يحول بيني وبينهم واد إذا جاءت الأمطار فيشق علي اجتيازه قبل مسجدهم فجئت رسول الله ﷺ فقلت له إني أنكرت بصري وإن الوادي الذي بيني وبين قومي يسيل إذا جاءت الأمطار فيشق علي اجتيازه فوددت أنك تأتي فتصلي من بيتي مكانا أتخذه مصلى، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: سأفعل
segments.english: Mahmud related that he heard ‘Itban ibn Malik al-Ansari, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who was among those who witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “I used to lead my people in prayer among Banu Salim. A valley lay between me and them; when the rains came, it was difficult for me to cross it toward their mosque. I came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said to him, ‘I have found my eyesight impaired, and the valley between me and my people flows when the rains come, making it difficult for me to cross it. I would like you to come and pray in a place in my house that I could take as a prayer place.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘I will do so.’”

segments.arabic: فغدا علي رسول الله ﷺ وأبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه بعد ما اشتد النهار فاستأذن رسول الله ﷺ فأذنت له فلم يجلس حتى قال أين تحب أن أصلي من بيتك فأشرت له إلى المكان الذي أحب أن أصلي فيه فقام رسول الله ﷺ فكبر وصففنا وراءه فصلى ركعتين ثم سلم وسلمنا حين سلم
segments.english: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, came to me in the morning after the day had advanced. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked permission to enter, and I gave him permission. He did not sit until he said, ‘Where in your house would you like me to pray?’ I pointed out to him the place where I liked to pray. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood, said the takbir, and we formed rows behind him. He prayed two rak‘ahs, then said the taslim, and we said the taslim when he did.”

segments.arabic: فحبسته على خزير يصنع له فسمع أهل الدار رسول الله ﷺ في بيتي فثاب رجال منهم حتى كثر الرجال في البيت، فقال رجل منهم ما فعل مالك لا أراه، فقال رجل منهم ذاك منافق لا يحب الله ورسوله،
segments.english: “I kept him for khazir that was being prepared for him. The people of the neighbourhood heard that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was in my house, and men from among them gathered until there were many men in the house. One of them said, ‘What has happened to Malik? I do not see him.’ One of them said, ‘He is a hypocrite who does not love Allah and His Messenger.’”

segments.arabic: فقال رسول الله ﷺ: لا تقل ذاك ألا تراه قال لا إله إلا الله يبتغي بذلك وجه الله، فقال الله ورسوله أعلم أما نحن فوالله لا نرى وده ولا حديثه إلا إلى المنافقين قال رسول الله ﷺ: فإن الله قد حرم على النار من قال لا إله إلا الله يبتغي بذلك وجه الله
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Do not say that. Do you not see that he has said, ‘There is no god except Allah,’ seeking by that the face of Allah?” He said, “Allah and His Messenger know best. As for us, by Allah, we see his affection and his conversation directed only toward the hypocrites.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “For Allah has forbidden to the Fire whoever says, ‘There is no god except Allah,’ seeking by that the face of Allah.”

segments.arabic: قال محمود فحدثتها قوما فيهم أبو أيوب صاحب رسول الله ﷺ في غزوته التي توفي فيها ويزيد بن معاوية عليهم بأرض الروم فأنكرها على أبو أيوب قال والله ما أظن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ما قلت: قط فكبر ذلك علي فجعلت لله علي إن سلمني حتى أقفل من غزوتي أن أسأل عنها عتبان بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه إن وجدته حيا في مسجد قومه
segments.english: Mahmud said: I related it to some people among whom was Abu Ayyub, the companion of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, during his expedition in which he died, with Yazid ibn Mu‘awiyah over them in the land of the Romans. Abu Ayyub objected to it, saying to me, “By Allah, I do not think the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ever said what you have said.” That weighed heavily on me, so I made a vow to Allah that, if He kept me safe until I returned from my expedition, I would ask ‘Itban ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, about it if I found him alive in the mosque of his people.

segments.arabic: فقفلت فأهللت بحجة أو بعمرة ثم سرت حتى قدمت المدينة فأتيت بني سالم فإذا عتبان شيخ أعمى يصلي لقومه فلما سلم من الصلاة سلمت عليه وأخبرته من أنا ثم سألته عن ذلك الحديث فحدثنيه كما حدثنيه أول مرة
segments.english: I returned and entered ihram for a Hajj or an ‘Umrah. Then I travelled until I reached Medina and came to Banu Salim. There was ‘Itban, an old blind man, leading his people in prayer. When he said the taslim from the prayer, I greeted him, told him who I was, and then asked him about that report. He related it to me as he had related it to me the first time.

comparisons.note: The Badr clause omits the selected with-the-Messenger phrase and its honorific; another Messenger honorific is represented by an asterisk. The eyesight request adds inability to lead prayer, and the food is glossed as meat soup. Loving and advising replaces the selected affection and conversation wording. These comparison choices must not overwrite the selected occurrence.

checkedBody: Narrated Mahmud bin Ar-rabi' Al-Ansari,

that he remembered Allah's Apostle and he also remembered a mouthful of water which he had thrown on his face, after taking it from a well that was in their house. Mahmud said that he had heard Itban bin Malik, who was present with Allah's Apostle in the battle of Badr saying, "I used to lead my people at Bani Salim in the prayer and there was a valley between me and those people. Whenever it rained it used to be difficult for me to cross it to go to their mosque. So I went to Allah's Apostle and said, 'I have weak eye-sight and the valley between me and my people flows during the rainy season and it becomes difficult for me to cross it; I wish you would come to my house and pray at a place so that I could take that place as a praying place.' Allah's Apostle said, 'I will do so.' So Allah's Apostle and Abu Bakr came to my house in the (next) morning after the sun had risen high. Allah's Apostle asked my permission to let him in and I admitted him. He did not sit before saying, 'Where do you want us to offer the prayer in your house?' I pointed to the place where I wanted him to pray. So Allah's Apostle stood up for the prayer and started the prayer with Takbir and we aligned in rows behind him; and he offered two Rakat, and finished them with Taslim, and we also performed Taslim with him. I detained him for a meal called "Khazir" which I had prepared for him.--("Khazir" is a special type of dish prepared from barley flour and meat soup)--

When the neighbors got the news that Allah's Apostle was in my house, they poured it till there were a great number of men in the house. One of them said, 'What is wrong with Malik, for I do not see him?' One of them replied, 'He is a hypocrite and does not love Allah and His Apostle.' On that Allah's Apostle said, 'Don't say this. Haven't you seen that he said, 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah for Allah's sake only.' The man replied, 'Allah and His Apostle know better; but by Allah, we never saw him but helping and talking with the hypocrites.' Allah's Apostle replied, 'No doubt, whoever says. None has the right to be worshipped but Allah, and by that he wants the pleasures of Allah, then Allah will save him from Hell." Mahmud added, "I told the above narration to some people, one of whom was Ab-u Aiyub, the companion of Allah's Apostle in the battle in which he (Ab-u Aiyub) died and Yazid bin Mu'aw7ya was their leader in Roman Territory. Abu Aiyub denounced the narration and said, 'I doubt that Allah's Apostle ever said what you have said.' I felt that too much, and I vowed to Allah that if I remained alive in that holy battle, I would (go to Medina and) ask Itban bin Malik if he was still living in the mosque of his people. So when he returned, I assumed Ihram for Hajj or 'Umra and then I proceeded on till I reached Medina. I went to Bani Salim and Itban bin Malik, who was by then an old blind man, was leading his people in the prayer. When he finished the prayer, I greeted him and introduced myself to him and then asked him about that narration. He told that narration again in the same manner as he had narrated it the first time."
comparisons.note: The meal is changed from being prepared to which I had prepared, with an added food recipe. The selected face-of-Allah wording is paraphrased as sake/pleasures, affection and conversation becomes helping and talking, and the first-person return becomes when he returned. Retain the complete Abu Ayyub objection and later Itban rechecking without these substitutions.

notes: Preserve the opening Mahmud memory, complete Itban account, Abu Ayyub objection, vow, Hajj-or-Umrah uncertainty and later rechecking through the final first-time comparison. Modern 1185/1186 split the opening memory from the remainder; do not shorten the entry at the Prophetic quotation.

The opening memory is visible, followed by the complete Badr frame, valley/eyesight request, visit, two-unit prayer, khazir, gathering, all quoted dialogue, Abu Ayyub objection, vow, Hajj-or-Umrah uncertainty and first-person return/rechecking. Fath al-Bari explains zaaama here as reported; the translation does not imply a false claim. Khazir is retained without a recipe. segments.english: ‘Abd al-A‘la ibn Hammad related to us. Wuhayb related to us, from Ayyub and ‘Ubaydullah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: اجعلوا في بيوتكم من صلاتكم ولا تتخذوها قبورا
